title: Signed in with a temporary profile

character.name: Hammad
character.personality: alarmed, thinks his files are gone

symptom: Windows says the user has been signed in with a temporary profile and his desktop looks empty
user_description: I logged in this morning and my desktop is empty and a message says I'm on a temporary profile. Where are all my files?

options.text: Tell him to carry on working in the temporary profile
options.why: Work saved in a temporary profile is usually lost when he signs out. He must not rely on it.

options.text: Delete his profile folder straight away
options.why: Dangerous. The profile still holds his real files, and deleting it could destroy them.

options.text: Tell him not to save important work, restart and sign in again, check free disk space, and if it persists repair or recreate the profile after backing up his files
options.why: The files are normally still in the original profile. A restart often fixes it, and a full disk is a common cause. If it persists, back up first so nothing is lost before repairing the profile.
Wipes everything and is not needed. The data is almost certainly still on the disk.

hints: What does 'temporary' tell you about work saved in this profile?
Are his real files gone, or just not loading?
What should you do before you change anything about a damaged profile?
real_world_tip: Reassure the user first. Their files are almost always still safe in the original profile folder.
